observation_refresh.why_no_epoch_c_snapshot: assert_repository_portfolio_snapshot.py refuses MIXED_SNAPSHOT_EPOCH when observed_at and the per-source issues/prs/workflows timestamps span more than --max-skew-seconds (default 300). This readback spans ~2400 s, so it cannot honestly become a snapshot.json epoch. A publication epoch needs one single-instant readback of issues + PRs + workflows before epoch C may be compiled.
observation_refresh.why_the_epoch_b_rows_were_not_rewritten: acceptance.json's per-packet digest is the frozen subject identity that every start_dependency/completion_dependency edge cites, and compile_repository_portfolio.py fails closed on any drift (verified 2026-08-22: mutating one packet's evidence.ceiling makes the compiler exit 1 with 'acceptance:ISSUE-559: digest mismatch'). Editing an observed_state in place would re-point every admitted dependency edge at a subject that did not exist at admission time. snapshot.json and acceptance.json therefore stay byte-frozen epoch-B observations, and the later truth lives here.
